newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Trust shares suspended on Tokyo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Trust shares suspended on Tokyo bourse.

text.p: Shares in Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd were suspended from trade on the Tokyo bourse on Wednesday amid unfounded rumours that the Japanese trust bank was planning hefty equity financing.
There were also vague market rumours, later denied by the bank, that it was suffering large currency losses and may withdraw from overseas operations, traders said.
The suspension triggered sales in other trust bank shares across the board, although the market's benchmark Nikkei 225 index ended the day up 80.61 points or 0.40 percent at 20,209.72.

Before the Tokyo bourse announced the suspension in mid-morning, the shares had been ask-only on rumours that the firm was considering equity financing worth some 100 billion yen ($840 million), brokers said.

"The talk of Sumitomo Trust's equity financing raised concerns over a supply glut in the market, as other banks might follow suit," said Hisao Suzuki, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Sumitomo later called a news conference at which it said it was considering financing but no details had been decided.
Sumitomo also denied other rumours that it has suffered large foreign exchange losses and that is withdrawing from overseas business, terming the talks "totally groundless".

Earlier in the week, underwriting sources said the bank was considering issuing euroyen convertible bonds worth some 100 billion yen ($840 million) in a bid to strengthen its asset base. But some said at that time that a lack of clear direction in the stock market may make the timing of the issue flexible. ($1=119 yen)
